shortName: University of South Carolina School of Medicine Columbia

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The SOM actively recruits and encourages applications from members of groups underrepresented in the medical profession. The diverse, representative membership of the Admissions Committee assures a thorough, sensitive review of each applicant. For more information, contact the Office of Admissions at 803-216-3625.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a Leave of Absence (LOA) through the Assistant Dean for Student Affairs to the LOA Committee.  Each student will meet with the LOA Committee and present materials for the committee's review.  The committee will make a recommendation to the dean.  The dean will meet with the student, consider all information and will inform each student within 10 working days of the decision regarding a LOA and of the process of review in the dean's decision.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students enrolled in the SOM may participate in a wide variety of University organizations, including those of specific interest to medical students.  Some of these include the SC Beta Chapter of Alpha Omega Alpha, the Medical Student Association, the American Medical Student Association, the American Medical Women's Association, the Student National Medical Association, the Christian Medical Association, IHI Open School, and multiple interest groups (dermatology, emergency medicine, family medicine, geriatrics, internal medicine, military medicine, obstetrics and gynecology, oncology, ophthalmology, pediatric, psychiatry, radiology, surgery, and wilderness medicine).  The University sponsors extensive programs in twenty one varsity sports. Its athletic teams, the Gamecocks and the Lady Gamecocks, compete as members of the Southeastern Conference of the NCAA Division 1A.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: On the grounds of the WJB Dorn VA Medical Center, the SOM is housed within the original buildings of the VA Hospital and located four miles east of the University of South Carolina main campus.  The historic buildings are reminiscent of Georgian architecture with their red bricks, white columns, and arched windows and are surrounded by a beautiful campus of spacious lawns, massive oak trees, and convenient parking.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The majority of USC SOM students choose housing in the area adjacent to the campus. Housing information can be obtained from the Student Affairs Office. Rents average $1200 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: In addition to student interest groups focusing on both gender and sexual minority students, the Committee on Women in Science and Medicine, and faculty/staff are trained as Safe Zone Allies to provide support to LGBTQ+ students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Students who have a documented disability may contact the Center for Well-Being and Academic Support. Visit https://sc.edu/study/colleges_schools/medicine/somc_student_resources/student_success_wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The School of Medicine Columbia is committed to creating healthy environments for our students. Students have access to a variety of health and wellness resources on both the VA campus and main USC campus. The Center for Well-Being and Academic Support at the School of Medicine is available to assist students in reaching their academic/career goals including a faculty coach and mental health counselor on-site. The Gamecock Pantry was created for students, by students. The pantry provides food assistance and other resources that enhance the community’s overall wellbeing.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The University of South Carolina School of Medicine - Columbia recognizes that its very creation was to reflect and serve the people of South Carolina. Therefore, state demographics and cultural history guides the school’s efforts to foster an environment where all persons have access to and feel engaged at School of Medicine Columbia. 
Excellence: We are committed to achieving the highest levels of personal and professional performance in all our endeavors.
Professionalism: We adhere to the highest standards of behavior guided by the values and practices of our professions.
Collaboration: We partner with individuals, teams, institutions, and communities to enhance the value of our efforts.
Compassion: We are resolute in our effort to relieve suffering and promote fairness.
Belonging: We are committed to building and sustaining an atmosphere of trust and respect in which all people can experience meaningful connections with others and are enabled to thrive and flourish.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Help sessions are offered before major exams and throughout a student's medical education. Tutoring is available through the Center for Well-Being and Academic Support.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: In their first and second year Introduction to Clinical Medicine course
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture-based, small groups, and problem-based learning
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin during the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Orientation begins one week before classes start and includes BLS training and study skills development.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Yes, for third year medical students.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The USC SOM offers a program of study that is designed to provide education and training in the art and science of medicine and to prepare students for a wide variety of medical career choices. Each of the first two years consists of fall and spring semesters that house basic science instruction paired with clinically relevant coursework. The correlation between basic and clinical science information in the first two years is emphasized by means of an interdisciplinary, four-semester Introduction to Clinical Medicine course continuum, during which students are exposed to patients in various inpatient, outpatient, community, and rural settings. Third year students rotate through required clinical clerkships in medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics-gynecology, family medicine, neurology, and psychiatry, plus 2 one-week electives. The fourth year is devoted to advanced clinical work, including 16 weeks of required rotations and a minimum of 16 weeks of elective rotations for a total of at least 32 weeks.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The USC SOM recognizes the need for additional primary care physicians and is committed to providing its students with a comprehensive clinical experience in all primary care disciplines.  Faculty from primary care disciplines teach extensively in all four years of the curriculum.  Required third year rotations include all specialties meeting the national definition of primary care (family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics).  Multiple urban and rural primary care offices and clinics including our regional campus in Florence, SC offer third and fourth year students opportunities to work closely with seasoned primary care practitioners.  Just under 50% of USC SOM graduates consistently elect to enter residency training in a primary care specialty.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Research programs and opportunities include a summer research program for medical students called SOAR.  This program provides research opportunities to USC medical students during the summer following their first year.  This is a eight-week, research experience provided by both clinical and basis science faculty which constitutes an important element of a well-rounded medical education.  The students learn how basic research can be translated from bench-to-bedside or vice versa.  The emphasis is for medical students to identify health and treatment-related problems, study mechanisms to solve them by carrying out basic research, and take the knowledge back to the clinic.  Annually, this program will accept a select group of rising second-year medical students to participate.  The details of the SOAR program can be accessed at  http://school.med.sc.edu/
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: MUSC - Florence, WJB Dorn VA Medical Center, Lexington Medical Center, McLeod Regional Medical Center, Prisma Health - Midlands, SC Department of Mental Health
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail for the first two years and clinical electives.  Numerical grading (A, B+, B, C+, C, D and F) for required M-III clerkships and M-IV Acting Internship.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of South Carolina SOM was established in 1977 and is located in the state's capital, Columbia. The school offers a wide range of educational and professional opportunities to its students, featuring a small class size, a state-of-the-art ultrasound curriculum, and a transformative educational experience to prepare learners to be leading health professionals and scientists. The school works closely with its four major teaching hospitals to provide students with a wide range of clinical experiences. In 2015 the SOM opened a regional campus for third and fourth year rotations in Florence, SC with a focus on professional leadership and rural training experience. In Fall 2027, the SOM will transition to its new Health Science Campus.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We serve the people of South Carolina and beyond through exemplary health and medical education, transformative research, and compassionate care for all. Since the core mission of the SOM is to serve the people of South Carolina, we primarily consider applicants who are residents of the state of South Carolina or applicants who are non-residents but have a significant tie or connection to our state. Our curriculum provides opportunities for our students to interact with practicing physicians during their first two semesters of medical school. These interactions occur as a part of a collaborative relationship with one of our clinical providers. The interactions supplement the experiences that students receive from working with standardized patients. The M2 curriculum also allows our students to utilize ultrasound technology to supplement the information that is learned during the systems-based curriculum of the second year of medical school. Part of the mission of the SOM is to provide compassionate care for all. Our students are exposed to various aspects of the Columbia and underserved community by volunteering at local shelters, by volunteering at the Free Medical Clinics, and by partnering with a variety of community service organizations that focus on the needs of the community. Additionally as a part of lectures and class discussions, our students have panels and presentations from persons that comprise our community as a part of their medical education. We strongly encourage all medical students to make a positive difference in their local communities.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Accelerated Undergraduate to M.D. program is a highly selective program for Honors College students and one of the most rigorous and challenging undergraduate programs offered by the University of South Carolina. The program includes completion of all pre-med and additional Honors requirements in three years and involves a significant research and thesis component. Medical school starts in the 4th year of the program and is completed in four years. Applications for the Accelerated Undergraduate to M.D. Program are by invitation only.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We require at least three letters of recommendation with a maximum of five letters. If your undergraduate institution prepares a Premedical Advisory Committee letter, we will accept that to fulfill the minimum letter requirements. We do not have requirements for the types of letters you must submit, but highly recommend two of these be from faculty in the sciences, so that we may better understand your abilities in the basic sciences. We recommend asking letter writers who know you well.  Some examples might be: a faculty professor at your undergraduate institution, a physician you have worked with closely or an employer. It is important that letter writers know you well and are able to comment on your work ethic, communication skills, and passion for medicine.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: In addition to two virtual 30-minute interviews, applicants will have a virtual meeting with our student ambassadors to hear about the SOM and ask questions. There is also a question and answer session with a representative of the Office of Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be virtual this year in our AMP application system.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Early Decision is open to residents of South Carolina only. The program is geared toward applicants for whom the USC SOM Columbia is their first choice and have a competitive application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee will also consider the trend of the scores.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
Although we do not have any course prerequisites, a strong preparation in the natural sciences is highly recommended including general biology, general chemistry, organic chemistry, and biochemistry. We also recommend coursework in the social sciences (anthropology, archaeology, economics, geography, history, law, linguistics, politics, psychology, or sociology). Further advanced studies in the biological, physical and/or chemical sciences are encouraged. Courses such as physics, histology, biochemistry, genetics, and molecular biology are also recommended. Courses are always valid for admission consideration and do not have an expiration. 

We give preference to applicants who will, upon enrollment, hold a bachelor’s degree. We occasionally admit students on the basis of 90 semester hours of outstanding undergraduate achievement.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Application updates can be made by applicants in their AMP portal during any time in the admissions process. However, application updates submitted after an applicant has interviewed will not impact their overall committee score from their interview day or their potential placement on the waitlist.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The SOM participates in all federally funded loan and scholarship programs. A SOM-sponsored low-interest loan program is available to students with proven need. Every effort is made to provide information and assistance to help students meet their financial obligations. Students seeking part-time employment during medical school should have the prior approval of the Associate Dean of Student Affairs.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is determined annual by the University of South Carolina's Board of Trustees.

medSchoolPrograms.info: In order to be qualified for the dual degree program, students must already be admitted to the M.D. program. After your first year in the program, you'll be able to apply for the dual degree. You should show an interest in both science and medicine by participating in prior medical research activities, such as internships in university departments, the NIH or CDC.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are notified in early April of their waitlist status. Not all applicants who interview are placed on the waitlist. Waitlist ranking is not disclosed to applicants.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Although we do not have any course prerequisites, a strong preparation in the natural sciences is highly recommended including General Biology, General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, and Biochemistry.

We also recommend coursework in the Social Sciences (Anthropology, Archaeology, Economics, Geography, History, Law, Linguistics, Politics, Psychology, or Sociology).

Further advanced studies in the Biological, Physical and/or Chemical Sciences are encouraged. Courses such as Physics, Histology, Biochemistry, Genetics, and Molecular Biology are also recommended.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Coursework is always valid for admission and does not expire.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The selection process involves the comparative evaluation and review of all available application data, including MCAT scores, undergraduate and postbac academic performance, letters of evaluation, and the results of personal interviews with Admissions Committee members.  The opportunity for admission is greatest for legal residents of South Carolina. Applications are only accepted from permanent residents or US citizens. The ultimate selection of a student is based upon a total and comparative appraisal of the applicant's suitability for the successful practice of medicine. The AMCAS application is used for preliminary screening. After this initial review, the Admissions Committee may extend an invitation for personal interviews. Each applicant is evaluated on the basis of individual qualifications without regard to age, race, creed, national origin, sex, or disability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Admissions Committee expects that applicants will have some health care experience at the time of application (i.e., volunteering at a free medical clinic or hospital, physician shadowing, medical scribing, EMT or CNA experience, etc.). We do not have a required number of shadowing hours. However, it should be significant enough that the applicant has a reasonable idea of what it means to pursue medicine.
